answers.question: The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?
answers.answer: No, there is not time for a 22-miler, and you do not need one. You already have a 20 (Sep 13) and a solid 17 (Sep 27) in the legs, and the aerobic gains from a long run take 2 – 3 weeks to show up. A 22 run inside two weeks of the race would add fatigue without adding fitness, and would eat into your taper. The right move now is a shorter long run with some marathon pace in it, then a true cutback the week after. You are ready for 3:45.

new.analysis:
## Why this week looks like this

You executed every session as planned last week, so I am taking the plan straight into the taper with no catch-up. The 17 at 9:59/mi with only +4.7 bpm of drift tells me the aerobic base is where it needs to be for 3:45.

The key session this week is the Sunday long run with marathon pace work, not raw distance. Target pace for 3:45 is about 8:35/mi, so I want you to spend time there with fresh-ish legs. This is a dress rehearsal for how 8:35/mi should feel in the first half of the race.

Wednesday stays as one quality day but shorter and at marathon pace rather than threshold. Threshold work peaks about 2 – 3 weeks out, so last week was the last hard one. From here, the job is to stay sharp without digging a hole.

Volume drops from 42 mi to about 36 mi, a gentle step down. Next week will drop again to around 28 mi, and race week will be very light. Keep the two strength or cross-training sessions in, but make them easy ones; this is not the time for anything new.

On the anxiety: it is normal, and the training does not need rescuing. Trust what you have banked and let the taper do its job.
